rulebook:
# ===== generic.yaml =====
# EDS Migration Rulebook — Generic layer
#
# Universal EDS authoring conventions. Good for any website migration.
# Loaded into every LLM-backed pipeline step alongside the project layer.
#
# --- Rule schema -----------------------------------------------------------
#   id:            stable slug, unique across all scopes (kebab-case)
#   scope:         generic | project | pipeline   (this file is always generic)
#   decision_type: convention | team-decision     (team-decision needs human sign-off)
#   category:      section | block | default-content | noise | structure
#   status:        confirmed | proposed           (only confirmed is applied in prod)
#   priority:      integer, higher wins within a scope (default 50)
#   trigger:       natural-language description of WHEN the rule applies (for the LLM)
#   decision:      natural-language description of the EDS mapping to produce (for the LLM)
#   rationale:     WHY — the EDS philosophy behind the rule (for humans + LLM context)
#   examples:      optional positive/negative illustrations
#   provenance:    where the rule came from (origin, added, version; sites for generic)
#
# scope: generic is EARNED, never self-declared by a scan. A rule reaches generic only
# after the same mapping is confirmed on >=2 distinct sites (provenance.sites) + sign-off.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

version: 1

rules:
  - id: background-container-is-section-style
    scope: generic
    category: section
    status: confirmed
    priority: 80
    trigger: >
      A visually cohesive zone has a background color, gradient, or image applied to a
      container that wraps two or more independent content items (e.g. a heading followed
      by a component, or several blocks stacked vertically).
    decision: >
      Do NOT treat the zone as a single block. Emit a section boundary around it, map each
      inner item to its own EDS item (default-content for headings/text, a block for each
      component), and represent the background via a section-metadata block with a style
      label — not as part of any block.
    rationale: >
      In EDS, backgrounds on a region of the page are section styles applied to the section
      wrapper as CSS classes. Wrapping content in a decorative block violates content-first
      authoring and blocks reuse of the inner components.
    examples:
      positive: Heading + tabs component sharing one lavender background → section(style) + H2 + tabs block.
      negative: A single card with its own background and rounded corners is a block, not a section.
    provenance:
      origin: hand-authored
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1

  - id: decorative-graphics-are-noise
    scope: generic
    category: noise
    status: confirmed
    priority: 70
    trigger: >
      Background dots, shapes, blobs, gradients, or ornamental imagery that carry no
      content meaning and exist purely for visual styling.
    decision: >
      Exclude from the block inventory entirely. If they belong to a section background,
      fold them into the section style; otherwise ignore.
    rationale: >
      Decoration is CSS, not content. Importing it as content items pollutes the inventory
      and the resulting EDS document.
    provenance:
      origin: hand-authored
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1

  - id: repeating-cards-are-one-block
    scope: generic
    category: block
    status: confirmed
    priority: 75
    trigger: >
      A grid or row of visually uniform items (cards, logos, features, stats, team members)
      repeating the same internal structure N times.
    decision: >
      Emit ONE block with N rows, not N separate blocks. Capture the per-item cell structure
      once as the block's row pattern.
    rationale: >
      EDS blocks are tables where each row is one item. A repeating grid is the canonical
      one-block-many-rows case.
    provenance:
      origin: hand-authored
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1

  - id: heading-then-component-same-section
    scope: generic
    category: default-content
    status: confirmed
    priority: 65
    trigger: >
      A heading (and optional intro paragraph) sits immediately above a component and shares
      the same visual region, with no intervening boundary or background change.
    decision: >
      Map the heading and intro as default-content, the component as its own block, both
      inside the same section. Do not absorb the heading into the block.
    rationale: >
      Headings that introduce a component are page content, authored as plain markdown above
      the block table. Absorbing them into the block reduces authorability and reuse.
    provenance:
      origin: hand-authored
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1

  - id: full-width-image-behind-text-is-section-bg
    scope: generic
    category: section
    status: confirmed
    priority: 78
    trigger: >
      A full-bleed image sits behind text/CTAs (classic hero) rather than appearing inline
      as a discrete content image.
    decision: >
      Represent the image as the section background via section-metadata, and map the
      overlaid text/CTAs as default-content and/or a block. Do not emit an image block.
    rationale: >
      A background image is decoration bound to the section, not an inline content asset.
    examples:
      negative: An image sitting in the normal content flow with text above/below it IS an image block.
    provenance:
      origin: hand-authored
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1

  - id: minimize-block-cells
    scope: generic
    category: block
    status: confirmed
    priority: 60
    trigger: >
      Deciding how many cells/columns a block table should have for a given component.
    decision: >
      Prefer the fewest cells that preserve the content. Combine an image + headings + text +
      links into a single cell when the decorate function can lay them out from markup order,
      rather than splitting each into its own cell.
    rationale: >
      EDS best practice favors minimal block tables; the decorate function derives layout from
      content structure, keeping authoring simple and blocks flexible.
    provenance:
      origin: hand-authored
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1

  - id: variant-is-css-not-new-block
    scope: generic
    category: block
    status: confirmed
    priority: 62
    trigger: >
      Two instances of the same block type differ only in appearance (color, alignment,
      spacing, emphasis) while sharing the same content structure and cell count.
    decision: >
      Treat as one block with a variant label appended to the block name (e.g. `hero (dark)`),
      not as a new block type. Variant labels become extra CSS classes.
    rationale: >
      EDS variants are CSS-only differentiators expressed as block-name labels. A new block
      type is only warranted when the content structure (cell count/shape) genuinely differs.
    provenance:
      origin: hand-authored
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1


# ===== knack.yaml =====
# EDS Migration Rulebook — Project layer (knack.com)
#
# Site-specific conventions discovered during THIS migration. Starts empty and grows as
# pipeline steps flag unknown patterns and a human reviewer confirms them.
# Loaded alongside generic.yaml; project rules take precedence on conflict.
#
# Same schema as generic.yaml. Every rule here MUST carry provenance pointing to the
# step + evidence it was discovered from, so a reviewer can trace why it exists.

version: 1

rules:
  # --- Example of a CONFIRMED discovered rule (human-accepted) ---------------
  - id: knack-cookie-notice-overlay
    scope: project
    category: noise
    status: confirmed
    priority: 90
    trigger: >
      A fixed-position cookie/consent overlay (small box, bottom-left, with a "Decline"
      control and third-party cookie copy) present on most pages.
    decision: >
      Exclude entirely from block inventory and section analysis. It is chrome injected on
      every page, not page content.
    rationale: >
      Consent overlays are global site chrome, never part of the imported document.
    provenance:
      origin: step2-longtail-scan
      evidence: overlay nodes rc3/rc4 recurring across nearly all captured trees
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1

  # --- Example of a PROPOSED rule awaiting human review ----------------------
  # Surfaced in a step report; NOT applied until a reviewer sets status: confirmed
  # (typically via the step's feedback.json).
  - id: knack-trust-badge-strip
    scope: project
    category: block
    status: proposed
    priority: 55
    trigger: >
      A horizontal strip of third-party rating badges (G2, Trustpilot, Capterra, etc.) each
      with a star score, appearing near the top of solution/landing pages.
    decision: >
      Candidate: emit as ONE "review badges" block with one row per badge. Needs confirmation
      that this recurs enough to warrant a dedicated block vs. a generic logo/card grid.
    rationale: >
      Recurs across multiple solution pages with identical structure; likely a reusable block
      rather than page-specific content.
    provenance:
      origin: step2-longtail-scan
      evidence: solution__solutions-*.json top zone, ~5x1 grid of badge+score
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1
  - id: knack-announcement-bar
    scope: project
    decision_type: convention
    category: noise
    status: confirmed
    priority: 88
    trigger: >
      A thin full-width bar at the very top of the page, above the nav, with a [bg:color]
      background and a short promo message + link (e.g. product announcement).
    decision: >
      Treat as global site chrome (announcement bar), exclude from the page's block inventory.
      If retained, model as a site-wide fragment, not per-page content.
    rationale: >
      Appears above the nav as a persistent marketing ribbon injected site-wide, not document
      content.
    provenance:
      origin: step2.1-longtail-scan
      evidence: "C06 rc1c1c1 [2x1][bg:color] above nav"
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1
  - id: leaked-css-text-node
    scope: project
    decision_type: convention
    category: noise
    status: confirmed
    priority: 72
    trigger: >
      A text node whose content is raw CSS/JS source (starts with a comment like /* ... */ or
      contains selector/property syntax), rendered visibly due to an unclosed style/script or
      authoring error.
    decision: >
      Exclude entirely. It is a source-leak artifact, never content.
    rationale: >
      Raw stylesheet text rendered into the page is a bug in the source site, not authorable
      content.
    provenance:
      origin: step2.1-longtail-scan
      evidence: "C06 rc1c2c2 '/* hero section starts*/ .grad...'"
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1
  - id: faq-accordion-block
    scope: project
    decision_type: convention
    category: block
    status: confirmed
    priority: 64
    trigger: >
      A vertical stack of uniform question rows (each a short heading, often with an expand
      affordance), typically under an 'FAQ' heading; visual tree marks the container
      [presentation] with N equal-height children.
    decision: >
      Emit ONE accordion block with one row per Q/A pair. The question is the row's first
      cell; the answer (may be collapsed/under-rendered) the second — confirm answer text via
      Phase 2.
    rationale: >
      FAQ accordions are a canonical reusable block; each item is one row, matching EDS table-
      per-item authoring.
    provenance:
      origin: step2.1-longtail-scan
      evidence: "C28 rc1c2c10c2 [presentation] with 5 uniform 60px rows"
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1
  - id: two-column-article-with-sidebar
    scope: project
    decision_type: convention
    category: structure
    status: confirmed
    priority: 66
    trigger: >
      A content page whose body is a [2x1] split of a wide primary text column and a narrower
      secondary column (sidebar: author box, related links, CTA, TOC).
    decision: >
      Map the primary column as default-content (headings, paragraphs, images in flow). Map
      the sidebar as its own block placed in the same section; EDS layout/CSS handles the two-
      column presentation. Do NOT emit the whole [2x1] as a single block.
    rationale: >
      The two-column split is layout, not a content unit. Sidebar contents are a reusable
      block; the article is plain authorable content.
    provenance:
      origin: step2.1-longtail-scan
      evidence: "C36 rc1c2c2 [2x1] article+sidebar; recurs on blog-post and case-study bodies"
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1


# ===== pipeline-rules.yaml =====
# EDS Migration Rulebook — pipeline-rules scope
# Auto-appended by promote-rules.py. See rules/README.md.

version: 1

rules:
  - id: underrendered-list-zone
    scope: pipeline
    decision_type: convention
    category: structure
    status: confirmed
    priority: 58
    trigger: >
      A category/listing page whose main zone is nearly empty in the visual tree (a single
      large bg zone with little text), indicating a card/list grid that fell below the
      minWidth capture threshold or loads lazily.
    decision: >
      Flag for Phase 2 targeted DOM extraction rather than concluding the page is empty. The
      zone is a listing block (cards/tiles), not a section background alone.
    rationale: >
      minWidth capture collapses fine-grained list items; treating the zone as empty would
      drop the page's primary content.
    provenance:
      origin: step2.1-longtail-scan
      evidence: "C12 rc1c2c2 [bg:gradient] 1280x507 with no child text"
      added: 2026-09-04
      version: 1

task: Using the rulebook, map this page's visual tree to EDS structure. Identify each block/default-content/section. Then flag any pattern NOT already covered by a confirmed rule as a candidate rule (status: proposed) with evidence. CONSTRAINTS on proposed rules: (1) scope MUST be 'project' (a site-specific convention) or 'pipeline' (an artifact of how WE captured/analyzed, e.g. content under-rendered by the minWidth capture) — NEVER 'generic'; a single site cannot justify a universal rule. (2) Set decision_type: 'convention' only for a near-objective mapping; use 'team-decision' when you are choosing among several valid EDS modelings, and name the alternatives you did NOT pick in the rationale. Output must match the verdict schema.
